b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic Sovereignty
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates 'The 12 Constitutional Principles of KnowledgeOS' in full: (1) Identity Preservation ('Identity survives transformation'); (2) Context Preservation ('Meaning = Object + Context'); (3) Evidence Integrity (claims require traceable foundations); (4) Authority Separation (evidence quality and source authority are separate dimensions); (5) Reasoning Transparency (every conclusion exposes Claim->Reason->Evidence); (6) Observation/Inference Separation (observed reality ≠ derived conclusion); (7) Contradiction Preservation ('Conflict is information. Not failure.'; state CONFLICTED when A=true and B=false); (8) Controlled Revision (knowledge evolves, history never deleted); (9) Temporal Truth (knowledge is always 'true as-of T', never a fake absolute present); (10) Non-Interference ('One dimension cannot silently corrupt another'; example: evidence changing does not automatically change authority); (11) Agent Accountability (every knowledge state remembers who knew/reasoned/asserted); (12) Semantic Sovereignty (imported knowledge preserves origin and assumptions).

group_evidence.why_grouped: an UNKNOWN-OBJECT-CANDIDATE row (batch B0027, source S1108) named these as alternative candidates for one piece of evidence. why_uncertain: Pattern of ungoverned self-modification may be tracked under a governance-invariant object already indexed, but no exact match confirmed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance decides. Assurance verifies. Engineering implements. AI assists.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the foundational four-way separation as one of the strongest invariants of KnowledgeOS; defines the Governance Runtime's responsibility (architecture changes, rule changes, exceptions, approvals, effective versions, accountability, decision records) as distinct from performing technical verification itself, with the governance architecture pipeline Change Proposal->Impact Analysis->Architecture Review->Governance Decision->{REJECT, APPROVE->Registry Version->Implementation->Assurance->{PASS,FAIL}} — 'approval precedes effectiveness, while assurance follows implementation.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Proposal ≠ Decision ≠ Implementation(Observation) ≠ Verification — four distinct domain concepts, not sequential statuses of one object.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the four-question model (what is proposed / what has been approved / what has actually been implemented / does implementation conform) and works four pairwise non-equivalences: Proposal ≠ Decision (an AI proposal to introduce a bounded context is not an ArchitectureDecision); Decision ≠ Implementation (Board approval ≠ code already changed); Implementation ≠ Conformance (only assurance establishes Conformant); Conformance ≠ Approval (code can technically conform to an unapproved architecture) — 'this distinction is extremely important.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: PROPOSED → APPROVED → IMPLEMENTED → VERIFIED — not sequential statuses of one object, but belonging to Proposal/Decision/Implementation/Verification respectively.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the GovernanceDecision aggregate (states DRAFT/SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW/APPROVED/REJECTED/SUPERSEDED, lifecycle organization-defined) and the Architecture Change Proposal schema (proposalId, subject, requestedChange, rationale, affectedArchitecture, impactAssessment, proposer, status), noting the proposal itself is not authoritative architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI-assisted impact analysis (Registry, repository, dependency graph, historical decisions, existing evidence) remains ImpactAssessment=Analysis, not a governance decision. Deterministic impact analysis (e.g. 'remove Module B' -> checker identifies 17 dependent modules) is strong evidence the AI can explain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines impact-analysis scope (Bounded Contexts, Dependencies, APIs, Events, Persistence, Security, Operations, Teams, Processes, Existing Exceptions) partly automated and distinguishes AI-generated impact summaries (still analysis, not decision) from deterministic impact checks (strong evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Actor ≠ Authority — e.g. Actor: Domain Architect, Authority: Architecture Board.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the Registry to identify the responsible authority per decision type (e.g. Architecture Principle Change->Architecture Board, Implementation Exception->designated approval authority), coming from the organization's actual governance model rather than being invented; distinguishes the person performing an operation (Actor) from the empowered organizational role/body (Authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision D42 basedOn ImpactAssessment, basedOn ArchitectureEvidence, basedOn RiskAssessment, produces ApprovedArchitectureVersion — decision traceability. Architecture Version → Decision → Proposal → Impact Analysis → Evidence → Original Observations — governed architectural memory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a decision to reference its supporting evidence and defines the full provenance traversal answering 'why was this architecture approved,' called 'governed architectural memory.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture v1.1 Status=APPROVED, Effective=2026-10-01. Before that date, v1.0 may remain applicable. ApplicableArchitecture = f(date, effectiveVersions, exceptions). A September-15 release must be evaluated against v1.0, not v1.1.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes temporal governance Architecture(t) with a worked historical-verification example showing which version applies to a release depending on effective dates, essential for correct historical audit; requires supersession (v1.0-supersededBy->v1.1) to keep v1.0 historically available, never overwritten; states approved decisions are historical — corrections produce new records rather than editing the original.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ProposalSubmitted, ReviewStarted, ImpactAssessmentCompleted, DecisionApproved, DecisionRejected, ArchitectureVersionApproved, ArchitectureVersionActivated, ArchitectureVersionSuperseded, ExceptionApproved, ExceptionExpired.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists a candidate ten-event governance vocabulary, to be derived from the actual lifecycle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Exception ≠ ArchitectureChange — approving that Module X may temporarily violate Rule R does not mean Rule R has changed. Exception{exceptionId,ruleId,subject,scope,rationale,approver,approvedAt,effectiveFrom,expiresAt,conditions}. Conditions prevent a blanket bypass.
a_rows_sample.statement: Elaborates the exception mechanism (Architecture Rule->Violation->Exception Request->Governance Decision->{REJECT->violation remains blocking, APPROVE->constrained deviation}), the exception schema, and worked conditional examples (e.g. allowed only if module remains isolated, no production deployment, migration completed by date X).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance Runtime defines Applicable Architecture → Assurance Engine verifies → Implementation; Assurance Finding flows back to Governance Runtime. GOVERNANCE → Architecture Rule → IMPLEMENTATION → ASSURANCE → {PASS, FAIL→FINDING→GOVERNANCE}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the Governance Runtime/Assurance Engine interaction and the resulting operational governance feedback loop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance must not consume only AI summaries ('the proposed change affects three contexts'); the authoritative basis is Evidence+Impact Assessment+Architecture Registry+Existing Decisions+Risk Information, with the AI explanation only a convenience layer.
a_rows_sample.statement: States governance decisions must rest on traceable evidence, not AI-generated summaries alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Context service reused for Developer→Engineering Context, Agent→Agent Context, Domain Architect→Architecture Context, Architecture Board→Governance Context. Context = f(Subject,Task,Role,Authority,Scope).
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Context Service to serve governance users (Architecture Board member context: Proposal, Current/Proposed Architecture, Impact, Findings, Exceptions, Evidence, Previous Decisions) and generalizes Context as role-sensitive — a powerful reuse of the platform across all actor types.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SubmitProposal, ReviewProposal, ApproveArchitecture, ApproveException, ActivateArchitecture — governance actions requiring authorization, distinct from technical actions (READ_NEXUS, DEPLOY_APPLICATION) but sharing the same Action/Authorization pattern. GovernanceAction ⊆ Action. ArchitectureDecision=APPROVED does not automatically mean DeveloperMayDeploy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes technical actions from governance actions while unifying them under one authorization infrastructure, and distinguishes a governance decision (defines/changes policy or architecture) from an authorization policy/action permission — the two domains interact but remain distinct (Governance Decision->Authorization Policy->Action Permission).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance Context {Proposal, Decision, Exception} → Governance Rules → Architecture Registry → Assurance Engine → Findings → Governance Review.
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the target Governance Runtime architecture diagram, and the resulting clean authority hierarchy (Governance defines->Architecture/Rules->Implementation->Runtime) paired with the upward evidence flow (Runtime->Observation->Evidence->Assurance->Governance), forming Governance<->Engineering feedback through evidence and assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance→PDF→Developer (typical anti-pattern) vs Governance→Machine-readable rule→Implementation→Deterministic verification→Evidence→Governance (KnowledgeOS target) — governance becomes operationally connected to engineering.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts the common architecture mistake of isolating governance from engineering with KnowledgeOS's operationally connected model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Machine detects pattern → Machine changes architecture (not the target) vs Machine→Observation→Analysis→Proposal→Human Governance→Decision (the target). AI can support proposal drafting, impact analysis, evidence synthesis, dependency analysis, alternative generation, risk identification, decision briefing, remediation suggestions; AI should not silently perform architecture approval, exception approval, governance policy creation, or authority delegation unless explicitly delegated under a governed model.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the opposite anti-pattern (machine unilaterally changing architecture) is equally forbidden, and enumerates AI's proper supportive role in governance versus what it must never silently perform.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Govern → Guide → Build → Observe → Assure → Learn → Govern.
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the closed-loop platform description (Govern=authoritative decision, Guide=governed context, Build=engineering, Observe=evidence, Assure=deterministic verification, Learn=validated knowledge, Govern=subsequent decisions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance decides what should be true. Registry records the declared architecture. Engineering implements it. Observation records what exists. Assurance determines whether it conforms. KnowledgeOS preserves the trace. AI accelerates reasoning across the loop, but does not silently become the authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 155 verdict, boxing the now-structurally-complete governance model in seven statements.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Platform ≠ Agent Harness ≠ Engineering Environment. Agent Harness makes an AI agent operate correctly inside a repository; KnowledgeOS Platform provides governed semantic engineering capabilities; Engineering Environment executes and exposes real engineering state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the three-layer runtime model with per-layer responsibilities and examples (Agent Harness: .claude/, .codex/, AGENTS.md, hooks, local scripts, session tooling; KnowledgeOS: Governance/Knowledge/Context/Evidence/Assurance/Authorization/Traceability; Engineering Environment: Git/CI-CD/Nexus/Kubernetes/Cloud/Applications/Infrastructure), and presents the resulting runtime topology diagram.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance: Nexus must satisfy R1; Agent memory: Nexus already compliant; Runtime observation: Nexus fails R1. Context Composer must preserve semantic status (AUTHORITATIVE EXPECTATION / LOCAL-UNVERIFIED / CURRENT OBSERVATION), not concatenate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Walks the context runtime sequence (Agent->API Gateway->Context Application Service->{Governance,Knowledge,Assurance,Evidence,Authorization queries}->Context Composer->ContextPackage->Agent); states the Context Composer is a composition mechanism, not an authority (Compose(AuthoritativeSources)->ContextPackage); worked example showing three conflicting sources must retain distinguishable semantic status rather than being merged, so the agent can reason correctly; the resulting ContextPackage is 'a view, not a new source of truth.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent → Reason → Recommendation. KnowledgeOS should not attempt to reproduce the agent's internal reasoning — it records task, context, recommendation, references, resulting action request.
b_rows_sample.statement: Walks the recommendation runtime (Agent->CreateRecommendation->Agent Application Service->Recommendation Aggregate->RecommendationCreated) and the action-request runtime (Agent->RequestAction->Action Application Service->Action Aggregate, Action.status=REQUESTED, nothing executed yet).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Instruction ≠ Enforcement. A malicious/buggy/misconfigured agent can ignore AGENTS.md's 'never deploy to production' — the authorization gate must exist inside the platform, not merely in agent instructions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Walks the runtime authorization gate (Action->Authorization->{DENY->STOP, ALLOW->Execute}) and argues this fundamental architecture point — a documented instruction is not a security boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Action → Execution Service → Engineering Port → Nexus Adapter → Nexus. Execution schema (executionId, actionId, externalReference, status, startedAt, completedAt).
b_rows_sample.statement: Walks the execution runtime and resulting Execution record schema, then the evidence runtime (Nexus->Observation->Nexus Adapter->Evidence Service->EvidenceRegistered, feeding Assurance/Graph/Audit/Context projections), the verification runtime (Evidence->Applicable Rule->Checker->Verification, checker may call the same or another adapter), event propagation to Graph/Context/Finding consumers processing independently, graph-projection creation of named edges (evaluates/appliesTo/supportedBy), and the finding runtime (Verdict=FAIL->Finding->FindingRaised->Governance/Workflow) — assembling the complete runtime loop as 'the runtime form of the Golden Trace.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Boundary 1 Agent<->KnowledgeOS. Boundary 2 KnowledgeOS<->External Engineering. Boundary 3 Governance<->Assurance. Boundary 4 Action<->Authorization. Boundary 5 Authoritative State<->Projections.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies five runtime boundaries, each requiring explicit contracts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zone A Agent Environment (untrusted for authority) → authenticated governed API → Zone B KnowledgeOS (governance boundary) → controlled adapters → Zone C Engineering Environment (operational authority).
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the trust-zone security architecture; states AgentOutput = Untrusted assertion until validated/governed (Zone A); Zone B determines what is authoritative/applicable/permitted/observed/verified (semantic control plane); Zone C is authoritative for actual runtime state, e.g. Nexus knows what repositories actually exist while KnowledgeOS knows what was observed and how it relates to governance — preventing KnowledgeOS from inventing operational truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Semantic/Governance Control Plane. Engineering systems = Execution/Operational Data Plane. Agent = Reasoning Actor. The agent recommends deployment but does not define whether deployment is allowed.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the control-plane/data-plane/reasoning-actor three-way separation and that the agent is explicitly not the control plane.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS unavailable ⇒ No execution (for governed high-risk actions). ExecutionPolicy = f(ActionRisk). LOW: FailOpen candidate. Governance-sensitive: FailClosed preferred.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines runtime resilience policy as action-sensitive (fail-open for low-risk local reads, fail-closed for governance-sensitive actions), formalized as ExecutionPolicy=f(ActionRisk); gives a four-level risk classification (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL) with worked examples (read Nexus config=LOW, modify staging=MEDIUM, deploy production=HIGH, change security policy=CRITICAL), the exact classification belonging to Governance/Security.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ContextRequest → Timeout → CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE rather than hanging. GET often safe to auto-retry; ExecuteAction requires idempotency/explicit retry semantics. Same ActionID ⇏ second physical execution.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires explicit timeout semantics for remote interactions and operation-specific retry rules, with ActionID providing stable execution identity so a retried Execute(A42) does not trigger a duplicate physical execution unless explicitly designed as repeatable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TraceID, RequestID, CorrelationID, ActorID, ActionID, ExecutionID available in logs/telemetry. GT-NEXUS-001 maps onto runtime telemetry (request context, query governance/assurance, request verification/action, authorization, execution, evidence, verification). TechnicalTrace ≠ SemanticTrace.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires runtime observability identifiers and distinguishes distributed request telemetry (technical trace) from engineering meaning (semantic trace) — the Golden Trace combines both without depending exclusively on either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Developer/Agent → HTTPS/API → KnowledgeOS Modular Application {Context,Governance,Knowledge,Assurance,Evidence,Authorization,Action} → {PostgreSQL, Outbox → Projection Workers → {Graph Index, Search Index, Context Cache}}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an initial deployment architecture without forcing microservices, with external adapters (Git/Nexus/CI/Kubernetes) connected from the same application, none needing to be a separate service in the first deployment; recommends Modular Monolith as the preferred first runtime architecture for clear domain boundaries, one deployable unit, simple local development, transactional simplicity, and easy Golden Trace debugging, with later decomposition into per-context services only when independent scaling/availability/security-isolation/organizational-ownership/deployment-independence actually justify it — deriving software topology from domain/organizational boundaries (Conway's Law) rather than inventing services first.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Existing mechanism → Defined boundary → KnowledgeOS contract. Claude/Codex become AgentAdapter_Claude/AgentAdapter_Codex sharing one KnowledgeOS Agent Contract, not owning GovernanceAuthority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps the existing ecosystem (Claude integration, Codex integration, AGENTS.md, hooks, memory, registry, deterministic checks, session logging, governance artifacts) onto contractualized roles without discarding them: AGENTS.md becomes the repository-level pointer (operating rules, local constraints, KnowledgeOS entry point) with enterprise authority remaining outside it; local hooks enforce local properties while enterprise governance checks additionally use the KnowledgeOS Assurance API (LocalFastCheck + GovernedAssurance); the session logger evolves toward Session->Action->Evidence (a CONNECT transformation from the delta map); existing deterministic-check scripts become CheckerAdapters bound to formal rules (e.g. Rule R-001) without needing immediate rewriting; presents the overall CURRENT->CONTRACTUALIZATION->KnowledgeOS APIs->Semantic integration->Golden Trace evolution staging, 'much less risky than a replacement project.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent harnesses are clients of KnowledgeOS, not alternate KnowledgeOS implementations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Article 3 -- Authority: 1. Evidence SHALL NOT constitute authority ... 2. Authority SHALL be assigned ... 3. Sources SHALL NOT be interchangeable
a_rows_sample.statement: Article 3 (Authority), 3 clauses: evidence/assessment/source SHALL NOT constitute authority; authority SHALL be assigned -- a recorded reference to a human act, never intrinsic or content-emergent; sources SHALL NOT be interchangeable (the means of acquisition SHALL be preserved -- sensor != expert statement != AI inference != historical document). Renders INV-001, INV-003, INV-KOS-Pramana-001. Failure if removed: a recorded reference self-authorizes; assessment becomes binding; source-role collapse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Result: only TWO of the five are fundamental architectural absences -- persistent epistemic identity and historical belief evolution
b_rows_sample.statement: LLM-comparison validation (5 candidates, validated not assumed): persistent epistemic identity -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (a stateless generative model cannot possess it by construction; scaffolding like RAG cannot grant identity, only look up stored identities); historical belief evolution -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (generation is stateless, no belief to evolve); provenance preservation, contradiction management, justification accountability -- each a DEGRADATION, not an absence (an LLM can be scaffolded to approximate each, weakly). Conclusion: the constitutional justification rests on exactly the two fundamental absences (mapping to laws 1 and 11), not a general 'LLMs are bad at X' claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel hypothesis K_OS=(A,T,P,E,I,S,X,R); goal is the smallest trusted kernel, not a maximal platform
a_rows_sample.statement: States the goal: the smallest executable system preserving all established mathematical properties, warning against building a huge platform containing every discussed concept. Proposes the candidate kernel K_OS = (A,T,P,E,I,S,X,R): Artifact, Epistemic Type, Provenance, Event, Invariant, State, Transformation, Rule/Policy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Eight removal experiments each yield FAIL, demonstrating each primitive is necessary
a_rows_sample.statement: Removal experiment 1 (Artifact identity): two identical claims C1=C2=p without identity make it impossible to determine which downstream decisions depended on which instance after one is invalidated -- FAIL, confirming ArtifactIdentity is fundamental. Experiment 2 (Type): content with no semantic type lets another process interpret 'system will fail tomorrow' as Fact with no way to detect illegitimacy -- FAIL, confirming Type is a kernel primitive. Experiment 3 (Provenance): ten agents producing the same statement without provenance yield an uninspectable SupportCount=10 -- FAIL, confirming provenance is indispensable. Experiment 4 (Event): knowledge changing from p to not-p with no recorded event leaves 'why did it change' Unknown -- FAIL, confirming event history is necessary for high-integrity evolution. Experiment 5 (Invariant): without invariant checking, P(A)=1.4 is structurally accepted -- FAIL, confirming Invariant must be executable. Experiment 8 (Policy): a decision auto-executing with no authorization rule -- FAIL, confirming governance policy belongs in the computational architecture (numbered out of sequence with experiments 7 and 9 in the source, which concern Transformation and Provider authority respectively).

a_rows_sample.anchor: State-projection removal experiment: PASS WITH PERFORMANCE FAILURE -- State is operationally, not logically, fundamental
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes State S_t can theoretically be reconstructed as a projection of event history S_t = Pi(E_1:t), so it is not necessarily fundamental in the mathematical sense. Experiment 6: storing millions of events with no efficient state projection makes every query require a complete replay -- theoretically computable but operationally inefficient -- 'PASS WITH PERFORMANCE FAILURE', concluding StateProjection is operationally necessary even though not logically fundamental.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicit-transformation and provider-authority removal experiments (implicit conversion and auto-verified LLM output both FAIL)
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: the system directly converting Prediction into Fact with no transformation record -- FAIL, confirming transformations must be explicit. Experiment 9: an LLM-produced Claim being automatically assigned Authority=Verified -- FAIL, confirming the provider must remain separate from epistemic authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Logical kernel K_L=(A,T,P,E,I,X,R) vs Operational kernel K_O=K_L+StateProjection+Indexes+Caching
a_rows_sample.statement: Having confirmed all eight primitives survive removal testing, freezes the candidate kernel K_OS = Artifact+Type+Provenance+Event+Invariant+State+Transformation+Policy, then refines the distinction between logical and implementation primitives: State is reconstructible from Events (not fundamental mathematically) but operationally valuable, giving Logical kernel K_L=(A,T,P,E,I,X,R) versus Operational kernel K_O = K_L + StateProjection + Indexes + Caching.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Trusted-kernel-smaller-than-the-platform principle; explicit exclusion list; Provider != Authority
a_rows_sample.statement: States the critical DDD principle: the trusted kernel should be smaller than the platform surrounding it -- AI systems, databases, graph engines, search engines, and statistical libraries should not all become part of the trusted semantic kernel. Explicitly excludes from the kernel, at least initially: VectorSearch, LLM, Embedding, PromptManagement, SpecificDatabaseTechnology, SpecificCloudProvider, SpecificAgentFramework -- these are replaceable computational providers, giving Provider != Authority (an LLM may provide a Hypothesis but gains no authority to declare VerifiedFact). Warns that a kernel dependent on one LLM or VectorDB becomes technology-bound, violating 'domain semantics dominate infrastructure'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel API sketch; Design-by-Contract transformation schema X=(InputType,OutputType,Preconditions,Procedure,Postconditions,ProvenanceRule)
a_rows_sample.statement: Sketches a conceptual kernel API (observe(), measure(), registerArtifact(), transform(), validate(), derive(), recordEvent(), queryProvenance(), evaluatePolicy(), authorize()) -- exact API left undesigned but semantic primitives clarified. Formalizes a transformation as X=(InputType, OutputType, Preconditions, Procedure, Postconditions, ProvenanceRule), 'much stronger than a generic function'; example: Measurement->Evidence with Preconditions=ValidUnit∧ValidSource∧ValidTimestamp and Postcondition=EvidenceHasProvenance. Experiment 10: an invalid-unit measurement attempted through Measurement->Evidence is Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 11: a transformation that creates an Evidence object but loses its source yields TransformationInvalid -- PASS, resembling Design by Contract (Precondition + Transformation + Postcondition), 'extremely suitable for deterministic assurance'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Composition requires Post(X1)⇒Pre(X2) and type match; new invariant I_CompositionalProvenance
a_rows_sample.statement: For X1:T1->T2 and X2:T2->T3, X2∘X1:T1->T3 is valid only if Post(X1)⇒Pre(X2). Experiment 12: composing X1 (Prediction->Claim) with X2 (Evidence->Decision) fails on type mismatch -- CompositionError -- PASS, showing the architecture is composable without one giant reasoning algorithm. Requires provenance to compose too: if e=V(m) and c=I(e), then Anc(c) superset-of Anc(e) union {m}. Experiment 13: two individually valid transformations whose composition loses the original measurement reference yields CompositionInvalid -- PASS, giving the new invariant I_CompositionalProvenance: valid transformations must preserve required ancestry across composition -- 'extremely important for AI pipelines'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Atomicity/transaction-boundary bridging mathematical invariants to software invariants
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes a transformation producing Artifact+Event+Provenance could be partially committed, risking ArtifactExists but ProvenanceMissing -- dangerous. Requires Artifact+Event+RequiredProvenance to commit as one atomic, consistent transition. Experiment 14: a database failure between artifact creation and provenance persistence should yield TransactionRollback or RecoverableIncompleteState, never silently appearing valid -- PASS. States the bridge explicitly: the mathematical invariant Provenance(a)!=empty becomes a database/transaction requirement -- 'Mathematical invariant -> Software invariant... the bridge we were looking for'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Event identity and partial (not invented total) ordering; Ordering != Causality
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires events to have identity id(e) and ordering semantics e_i≺e_j where relevant, noting a distributed system may lack a global total order, requiring a PartialOrder instead (e.g. e1≺e3 and e2≺e3 without e1≺e2). Experiment 15: two causally-unordered distributed events should not have an invented e1<e2 -- OrderingUncertain -- PASS, relevant when integrating Git/Jira/CI/production telemetry/human decisions/AI outputs with differing clocks (Timestamp != CausalOrder). Notes a Lamport-style logical clock establishes e1->e2 only when causality is actually known; L(e1)<L(e2) does not mean e1 caused e2 -- Ordering != Causality. Experiment 16: an agent claiming Cause(e1,e2) purely from L(e1)<L(e2) is Rejected -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hexagonal kernel architecture; AI-provider and database-technology replacement preserve core invariants
a_rows_sample.statement: Depicts the kernel (Artifact, Epistemic Type, Provenance, Event, Invariant, Transformation, Policy, State Projection) surrounded by AI/ML Engine, Statistics, Causal Engine, and External Systems -- 'very close to Hexagonal Architecture' (Core + Ports + Adapters: LLMAdapter, GitAdapter, JiraAdapter, DatabaseAdapter, StatisticalEngineAdapter), with the domain kernel not depending on concrete technologies. Experiment 17: replacing LLM_A with LLM_B leaves KnowledgeOS epistemic semantics unchanged -- CoreInvariantPreserved -- PASS. Experiment 18: replacing relational storage with another storage implementation leaves KnowledgeOSCore behaving equivalently as long as semantic contracts hold -- PASS, demonstrating architectural independence from infrastructure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel execution loop; AI as computational participant not epistemic authority; KnowledgeOS = Governed Semantic Kernel + Computational Providers
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the minimal executable kernel loop Input -> Classify -> Validate -> Transform -> CheckInvariants -> Commit -> ProjectState, worked through a Measurement->Evidence example, and notes an AI (e.g. for Evidence->Hypothesis) may perform generation while the kernel still controls InputType, OutputType, Provenance, Policy, Persistence -- 'AI is a computational participant, not the epistemic authority', 'probably one of the most important architectural conclusions so far'. Concludes KnowledgeOS should not be designed as LLM+Memory but as Governed Semantic Kernel + Computational Providers, with the LLM one provider among several. States the kernel's basic operations are O(n)/O(n log n) for practical cases, with LLM/large-scale statistics/causal models/massive data processing as optional providers -- 'KnowledgeOS does not inherently require large-scale infrastructure'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 70 verdict: minimal kernel as a credible software architecture target; opens Step 71 on compositional correctness
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 70 -- PASS: a minimal kernel requires typed artifacts, provenance, explicit transformations, eventual state, executable invariants, and policy-controlled transitions, with everything else composable around it -- 'the mathematics can be compiled into a small set of executable semantic contracts'. Describes the current architecture as KnowledgeOS = SemanticKernel + KnowledgeGraph + InferenceEngines + AI Agents + Governance + External Adapters, with the Semantic Kernel as the trusted center. Poses the remaining question of whether a sequence of individually valid transformations remains valid when composed into a large workflow (Valid(X1) and Valid(X2) do not automatically imply Valid(X2∘X1)), opening Step 71 (Compositional Correctness of KnowledgeOS, already covered as S0968) to examine ContractComposition, InvariantComposition, ProvenanceComposition, TransactionComposition, WorkflowCorrectness, and AgentComposition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel updated to add Identity: K_OS=Artifact+Type+Identity+Provenance+Event+Invariant+Transformation+Policy
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues Identity should now be considered a kernel-level concern (trustworthy provenance requires attribution), while cryptographic implementation (PKI/HSM/KeyVault) remains infrastructure, not kernel-native. Updates the kernel to K_OS = Artifact + Type + Identity + Provenance + Event + Invariant + Transformation + Policy, with State as the operational projection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reduction problem: which of the 48-step concepts are primitives versus structures over primitives?
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the reduction question against the accumulated concept list (Entity, State, Observation, Evidence, Claim, Identity, Semantics, Provenance, Uncertainty, Causality, Event, Policy, Decision, Action, Outcome, Learning): which are primitives, and which are structures over primitives? Proposes a first grouping into Core primitives (Entity, State, Event, Observation), Epistemic structures (Evidence, Claim, Uncertainty), Semantic structures (Identity, Meaning, Context), Relational structures (Provenance, Dependency, Causality), Governance structures (Policy, Authority, Decision), Operational structures (Action, Outcome), and Evolution structures (Learning, Revision, Drift).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Entity, State, Event, Observation re-derived: e=(id,type,attributes); DomainEvent vs ObservationEvent; O=(source,t,value)
b_rows_sample.statement: Questions whether Entity is truly primitive: e=(id,type,attributes) makes 'Entity' arguably a semantic abstraction over Identity+State, though keeping it as a domain primitive remains useful for DDD identity-bearing objects. State is fundamental: S_t=(x_1,...,x_n). An event is a state transition or external report, distinguished into DomainEvent (e_t: S_t->S_{t+1}) versus ObservationEvent. An observation is O=(source,t,value) -- 'a source reported or measured something at a particular time', not necessarily a correct interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence = Observation+Relevance+Context (not a primitive); Claim as uncertain-truth proposition; Probability vs EpistemicConfidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Reduces Evidence to Evidence = Observation + Relevance + Context -- 'Evidence need not be a fundamental primitive; it is a qualified observation'. Defines Claim as a proposition C: Omega -> {True,False} whose truth status is realistically uncertain. Proposes treating uncertainty as a general epistemic annotation U(C) (possibly P(C), Confidence(C), or Interval(C), not assumed probabilistic), then makes an explicit correction: Confidence used loosely earlier was too broad -- a probability P(H)=0.8 is not necessarily the same as a subjective confidence score Confidence(H)=0.8, so KnowledgeOS should distinguish Probability from EpistemicConfidence -- 'an important normalization'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity as Entity->Identifier mapping; Meaning as contextual (DDD bounded-context-relative); governed context translation T_12
b_rows_sample.statement: Identity(e)=id, a mapping Entity -> Identifier, itself potentially uncertain under uncertain entity resolution. Meaning(c,t,context) is inherently contextual: Meaning(x,c1) may differ from Meaning(x,c2) across the set of bounded contexts C; a translation T_12: Model_1 -> Model_2 maps concepts across contexts and should itself be governed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance and Causality reduced to typed relations; Supports != Causes != DependsOn
b_rows_sample.statement: Provenance Prov(C)={E_1,...,E_n}, generalized to a DAG-shaped Prov(x); reduced to a relation, not a primitive object: Supports(E,C), DerivedFrom(C1,C2). Causality is another relation Causes(A,B), explicitly not to be conflated with Supports(A,B): Supports != Causes. Software dependency DependsOn(A,B) is yet another relation, and DependsOn != Causes -- a system may technically depend on a component without that component being the causal reason for a given outcome. Consolidates a typed relation set R={Supports, DependsOn, Causes, Identifies, MapsTo, Contradicts, Precedes} that must remain typed: collapsing everything into a generic RelatedTo(A,B) loses semantics and could let an AI infer RelatedTo=>Causes, 'recreating one of the fundamental problems we eliminated in Step 43'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy, Authority, Decision, Action, Outcome, Learning, Revision, Drift reduced
b_rows_sample.statement: Policy(s,a)->{Permit,Deny}, generalized to P: State x Action -> DecisionConstraint. Authority(actor,d) is distinct from Policy: a policy may permit an action while the actor still lacks authority. Decision D:(K,S,Policy)->A, distinguishing DecisionProposal from AuthorizedDecision. Action A: S_t->S_{t+1} (or P(S_{t+1}|S_t,A) stochastically). Outcome is an observed post-action consequence, possibly multiple: A->{O_1,...,O_n}. Learning L:(K,E)->K' is 'not itself knowledge... a transition operator over knowledge states' -- 'an important reduction'. Revision K_t->K_{t+1} is likewise a state transition, and Drift(K_t,K_{t+1}) or Drift(P_t,P_{t+1}) is a detected difference, 'not a primitive'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate mathematical kernel K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Π,A) and derived-structure mapping
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates into a candidate kernel K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A): E=entities, S=states, T=temporal/event structure, O=observations, P=propositions, R=typed relations, Pi=policies, A=actions -- then re-freezes it slightly differently as the eight-element set P={Entity,State,Event,Observation,Proposition,Relation,Policy,Action}, with everything else required to be expressible as Structure(P). Gives explicit derivations: Evidence subset-of O x Context; Claim subset-of P; Prov subset-of R; Cause subset-of R; Identity: E->ID; Learning: K_t->K_{t+1}; Decision: (K,S,Pi)->A; and later restated as Evidence=QualifiedObservation, Claim=Proposition, Identity=EntityIdentityRelation, Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation, Causality=TypedCausalRelation, Decision=PolicyConstrainedActionSelection, Outcome=PostActionObservation, Learning=KnowledgeStateTransition, Drift=Distribution/StructureDifference. Proposes a standing test for every future concept X: is X a new primitive or derivable from the kernel -- if derivable, X not-in P, 'this prevents uncontrolled architectural expansion'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Finite representability; polyglot storage (not everything is a graph); domain/infrastructure (hexagonal) separation
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the architecture is computable in principle: a finite knowledge state K=(V,E,R,Metadata) (a typed temporal graph plus domain state) is representable since |Entities|,|Relations|,|Events| are finite at any point in time. Depicts a graph-shaped domain sketch (Entity-hasState->State, -observedBy->Observation, -participates->Event->Proposition->{supports,causes,contradicts}->Decision->Action->Outcome) but explicitly corrects that not everything should be a graph: graphs suit relationships/provenance/dependencies/causal structure but not transactional state, large numerical arrays, time series, documents, or statistical models -- KnowledgeOS should be polyglot. Defines Storage(K) without requiring Storage=GraphDatabase (possible backends: RelationalDB, GraphDB, ObjectStore, VectorIndex, TimeSeriesDB), consistent with Hexagonal Architecture: the domain defines Meaning, infrastructure defines Representation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Core architecture runs on a normal PC; heavy computation is optional/delegable acceleration
b_rows_sample.statement: Answers directly: yes, the core architecture (typed graph operations, relational queries, event processing, deterministic rules, many statistical calculations, provenance traversal, state-machine verification, moderate simulations) can run on a normal PC; workloads like massive embeddings, LLM inference, huge graph analytics, large Monte Carlo simulation, large-scale optimization, or enterprise-wide event histories may need larger/distributed infrastructure, but these are 'implementation-scale concerns, not contradictions in the mathematical architecture'. Concludes CoreKnowledgeOS should remain computationally lightweight, with external compute as OptionalAcceleration -- the domain layer should not know GPU, only InferenceRequest; infrastructure decides LocalCPU vs RemoteGPU. Depicts a clean architecture: Domain (Knowledge/Decision/Governance) -> Ports/Contracts -> {Local DB, Graph Store, Compute Engine (Local/Remote)}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MathematicalModel, SoftwareArchitecture and InfrastructureArchitecture are related but distinct layers
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates three related-but-non-identical layers: the Mathematical model defines what exists and what relationships mean; Software architecture defines where behavior lives and how contexts interact; Infrastructure defines where computation and persistence execute -- 'this separation is essential'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Formal reduction result: most of the 48 concepts are derived structures, not independent primitives
b_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes: many of the 48 concepts are not independent primitives but derived structures -- 'good news... the architecture is becoming simpler'. Freezes the candidate kernel P={Entity,State,Event,Observation,Proposition,Relation,Policy,Action}. States the 49-step journey converges toward Small kernel + Typed relations + Temporal state + Epistemic annotations + Governed transitions, and gives the compact high-level equation KnowledgeOS = State + Evidence + Relations + Inference + Policy + Decision + Evolution, more formally K_{t+1}=Learn(K_t,Observations_t,Events_t,Policies_t,Outcomes_t), A_t=Decision(K_t,S_t,Policy_t), S_{t+1}=F(S_t,A_t,U_t). States the most important discovery of Step 49: KnowledgeOS does not need a gigantic mathematical ontology, only 'a small, rigorously typed kernel over which richer domain concepts can be constructed'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 49 primitive-reduction model (all PASS)
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) can Evidence exist without Observation? No => Evidence is derived; (2) can Provenance exist without Relations? No => Provenance is relational structure; (3) can Causality be represented as generic RelatedTo? Not safely => Causes must be a typed relation; (4) can Learning be represented as a static object? Not adequately => it is a transition K_t->K_{t+1}; (5) can Decision be separated from Action? Yes => Decision->Action, preserving authorization/dry-run semantics; (6) can Outcome be treated as Decision? No => an outcome is a post-action observation; (7) can Unknown be represented as False? No => the three-valued epistemic distinction remains necessary; (8) can approximate computation be represented as exact? No => computation status must be retained; (9) can every theoretical KnowledgeOS question be computed exactly? No => undecidability/complexity impose limits; (10) does mathematical complexity require special hardware? Not necessarily => complexity determines resource requirements, not model validity; (11) can the same domain model run on local or distributed infrastructure? Yes, if ports/contracts isolate infrastructure; (12) can a new concept be added without increasing the primitive kernel? Yes, if derivable from existing primitives.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Opens Step 50: attempt to break the model via a KnowledgeOS Reference State Machine and adversarial injection
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the architecture should stop expanding temporarily and undergo a formal consistency audit: do the primitives and invariants actually permit all previously defined behaviors? Proposes constructing a KnowledgeOS Reference State Machine over Observation -> Evidence -> Claim -> Validation -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> Learning, then deliberately injecting contradiction, stale evidence, identity collision, semantic mismatch, causal misclassification, unauthorized action, model drift, feedback amplification, incomplete information, and computational timeout -- framing Step 50's objective as stronger than another conceptual PASS: 'attempt to break the model', with survival taken as substantially stronger evidence of internal coherence and readiness to move from theory to executable reference architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Critical discovery: mathematical model coherent, implementation needs additional operational contracts; three-layer architecture
b_rows_sample.statement: After 50 adversarial tests find no contradiction in the mathematical kernel, states the critical discovery: the mathematical model is coherent, but the implementation requires additional operational contracts -- 'exactly what a good formal audit should reveal'. Lists newly identified mandatory contracts: Event processing (Idempotency, Ordering, Replayability); Governance (PolicyPrecedence, PolicyBinding, AuthorityBinding); Relations (TypedRelations); Concurrency (ConcurrencyControl); Models (ModelArtifactIdentity); Provenance (AcyclicDerivation) -- explicitly 'not new conceptual primitives... constraints on implementation'. Gives a three-layer architecture: Layer 1 Mathematical kernel (Entity, State, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action); Layer 2 Epistemic/semantic structures (Evidence, Identity, Meaning, Provenance, Uncertainty, Causality); Layer 3 Operational contracts (Authorization, Concurrency, Idempotency, Versioning, Replay, PolicyBinding, ModelBinding).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Primitive-ownership audit: no primitive requires a global 'KnowledgeOS' owner
b_rows_sample.statement: Tests whether every mathematical primitive has a legitimate context owner: Entity identity -> Domain/Semantic context; State -> owning domain context; Event -> owning domain context; Observation -> Evidence; Proposition -> Knowledge; Relation -> owning relation context; Policy -> Governance; Action -> owning domain/operation context. Concludes 'no primitive requires a global owner called KnowledgeOS. That is a very healthy result.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pratyaksa Perception ... Anumana Inference ... Upamana Comparison ... Sabda Testimony ... KnowledgeOS Parallel: Observation, Reasoning from evidence, Pattern matching/analogical reasoning, Authority/expert testimony
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the four Nyaya pramanas with a proposed KnowledgeOS parallel mapping and notes perception is treated as fundamental because the other three depend on prior cognition; concludes KnowledgeOS's existing Evidence/Authority/Reasoning distinctions could be given a structured epistemological framework via this mapping.

a_rows_sample.statement: Cites a 2026 preprint (Sathish, University of York, via Zenodo) fine-tuning an LLM on a six-phase Navya-Nyaya methodology (Samshaya/Pramana/Pancha Avayava/Tarka/Hetvabhasa/Nirnaya), reporting 100% semantic correctness on 10 examples but only 40% strict format adherence, interpreted as evidence the methodology teaches genuine reasoning rather than template-filling.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unlike Western formal logic (divorced from epistemology), Nyaya integrates logic with explicit knowledge sources.
a_rows_sample.statement: Comparative table contrasting Tarka Shastra/Nyaya against Western epistemic logic across knowledge sources, reasoning structure, contradiction handling, authority, doubt, and goal, concluding Nyaya offers a more integrated epistemology+logic+authority framework than Western formal logic alone.

a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate invariant TARKA-001: every knowledge claim must be explicitly grounded in a valid knowledge source (perception/inference/comparison/testimony); classified 'strong candidate', pending validation against EKS/PKS/AIP evidence.

a_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates six forbidden transitions derived from Tarka Shastra, each paired with the Nyaya parallel that forbids it (apramana, hetvabhasa, tarka-is-apramana, unclassified samsaya, dustarka, the five circular-tarka fallacies).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The system must not flatten: Sensor observation = Expert statement = AI inference. That would violate epistemic identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the four-pramana mapping (Pratyaksa/Anumana/Upamana/Sabda -> Observation/Reasoning-derived/Analogy/Authority) and derives a constraint: knowledge sources have different epistemic roles and must not be flattened into equivalence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sensor reading != Expert assessment != Logical inference != Historical document ... INV-KOS-Pramana-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the means by which knowledge was acquired because validity depends on the epistemic method of acquisition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the four pramanas and proposes INV-KOS-Pramana-001, arguing evidence must include Evidence Type + Acquisition Method + Reliability Conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Many AI systems collapse: Observed and Inferred. KnowledgeOS cannot... INV-KOS-InferenceBoundary-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the distinction between directly observed knowledge and knowledge derived through reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the smoke/fire anumana example to argue inference is a transformation, not a source, and proposes INV-KOS-InferenceBoundary-001 to keep Observation and Inference structurally distinct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should be built around Pramana (Knowledge Sources), not Knowledge Objects... Knowledge is not primarily a stored thing. Knowledge is the output of a reliable process.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a modern Data->Information->Knowledge model with a Nyaya-inspired Object->Knowledge Source(Pramana)->Valid Cognition->Successful Action pipeline, arguing this book gives 'the runtime architecture of epistemic operations' as opposed to the prior book's 'logic of justification'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Source Registry ... perception: reliability: high_for: [infrastructure_state, runtime_metrics] ... The book identifies four knowledge sources: perception, inference, analogy, testimony
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes adding a 'Pramana Registry' / Knowledge Source Registry with a YAML schema recording per-source reliability conditions, alongside existing Evidence/Observations/Decisions/ADRs/Governance records.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Word is what is instructed by a trustworthy person (apta)... Word + Reliable Source + Correct Understanding = Knowledge ... KnowledgeTransmission: source, utterance, semantic_context, receiver, cognition, trust
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'Sabda-Pramana as KnowledgeOS Communication Protocol': a message becomes knowledge only when the source is trustworthy, communication succeeds, and the receiver correctly understands it; models this as a KnowledgeTransmission schema.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge claims must be traceable to their generation process ... Error is a modified version of truth, not a distinct state ... Default trust is the epistemic default ... trust by default and doubt only on reason.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traceable Generation pattern (Nyaya pramana): every knowledge unit records its source/generation conditions; error is modeled as a misplacement rather than a distinct category; the epistemic default is trust, with doubt requiring a reason.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `EvidenceLinks` (l. 209) carries *"evidence references + **acquisition method** + reliability conditions."* **Acquisition method is already there.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Session 1 claims three separate carriers an evidence/claim reference may need: route (S1-F035, by what epistemic means was this obtained, e.g. pratyaksa vs upamana), acquisition procedure (S1-F030), and role (S1-F029). This review disputes the count: EvidenceLinks (l.209) already carries evidence references plus acquisition method plus reliability conditions -- acquisition method is already in law -- and route is very close to acquisition method, so whether they are one carrier or two is the same semantic-denotation question left open at two prior reviews (S2-R-F029, S2-R-F030). The defensible composite is smaller: one carrier already in law (acquisition/route, possibly one thing) plus one genuinely absent carrier (role).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pramāṇa describes the route to knowledge. Verification/refutation describes how the resulting claim is tested.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes pramana (route to knowledge acquisition) from verification/refutation (how a resulting claim is subsequently tested), combining both into a pipeline: Knowledge Claim -> Pramana -> Epistemic Tests {Verify, Repeat, Refute} -> Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REALITY -> OBSERVATION -> PRAMĀṆA LENS -> {perception, inference, testimony} -> CLAIM -> CRITICAL THINKING -> {assumptions, alternatives, defeaters} -> EVALUATION -> {evidence, uncertainty, provenance} -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> TIME -> K(t)->K(t+1)->K(t+2) -> META-KNOWLEDGE -> ZERO
b_rows_sample.statement: Synthesizes all lenses read so far into one combined pipeline from Reality through the Pramana lens (perception/inference/testimony), Claim, Critical Thinking (assumptions/alternatives/defeaters), Evaluation (evidence/uncertainty/provenance), Knowledge State evolving over time (K(t)->K(t+1)->K(t+2)), Meta-Knowledge ('what do we know about what we know?'), terminating in Zero (invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVIDENCE -> PRAMĀṆA/PROVENANCE -> EVALUATION -> {T, F, BOTH/NEITHER} -> KNOWLEDGE STATE -> LEGITIMACY -> GOVERNANCE ... Legitimacy should not manufacture a truth value.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Evidence->Evaluation->Legitimacy architecture with an explicit T/F/Both-Neither evaluation branch feeding Knowledge State, then Legitimacy, then Governance, asserting Legitimacy must act on the epistemic state per constitutional rules rather than manufacture a truth value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lens 1 — Ganesha ... Lens 10 — Statistical
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a ten-lens extraction engine, each with a name and defining question: Ganesha (definition -- what exactly is the proposition), Pramana (epistemic origin -- how did we obtain it), Leonardo (critical discovery -- assumptions/alternatives/contradictions), Krishna (purpose -- what decision this knowledge serves), Shani (invariants -- what must not be violated), Zero (invariant structure -- what remains across representations/perspectives), Dhatu (generation -- what transformations generate the observed state), Temporal (evolution -- how the knowledge state changes through time), Hofstadter (self-reference -- what the system knows about its own knowledge), Statistical (quantification -- evidence/uncertainty/convergence/contradiction measurement).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Textual quotation ≠ philosophical interpretation ≠ historical assertion ≠ scientist's personal opinion ≠ physical theory ≠ empirically established result ... "Multiverse exists only in Hindu Cosmology" is an article headline/claim, not something demonstrated by the material presented.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Pramana lens to the source article itself, distinguishing six non-collapsible statement kinds it contains (textual quotation, philosophical interpretation, historical assertion, scientist's personal opinion, physical theory, empirically established result); a physicist's stated belief that a cyclical universe is 'most probable' is testimony/opinion, not established cosmology, and the headline claim 'multiverse exists only in Hindu Cosmology' is not demonstrated by the material presented.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Science -> Method/validation | Time -> Temporal knowledge | Logic -> Epistemic state space | Epistemology -> Knowledge acquisition | Cosmology -> World model | Eschatology -> Terminal state/transformation ... KnowledgeState = (Method, Time, Logic, Epistemology, WorldModel, TerminalState)
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps the six source articles processed across this series to six abstract dimensions (Science->Method/validation, Time->Temporal knowledge, Logic->Epistemic state space, Epistemology->Knowledge acquisition, Cosmology->World model, Eschatology->Terminal state/transformation), formalizing a series-closing tuple KnowledgeState=(Method,Time,Logic,Epistemology,WorldModel,TerminalState).

b_rows_sample.anchor: They weren't producing competing architectures. They were probing different dimensions of the same boundary. ... Dhātu ... Karaka ... Pramāṇa ... Statistical ... Topological ... DDD ... Shani ... Ganesha ... Leonardo ... Krishna ... a multi-dimensional boundary discovery methodology.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the ten accumulated lenses (Dhatu/linguistic: how is meaning expressed; Karaka: what relationships exist between participants; Pramana: on what basis can something be accepted as knowledge; Statistical: how much uncertainty/evidence/structure can be inferred; Topological: shape/connectivity of the knowledge space; DDD: who owns which meaning/invariant; Shani: what must never be violated; Ganesha: do we actually understand the concept; Leonardo: what assumptions are hiding; Krishna: why does this boundary exist) as jointly constituting one multi-dimensional boundary-discovery methodology rather than competing architectures.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation and inference are different obligations with different invariants. The Kernel is a preservation boundary. Possible-worlds semantics, pramāṇa, statistical inference and algorithmic knowledge are all regimes that read the record. That framing satisfies §28 while giving F-4 a real answer: the Kernel's non-negotiable job is to keep the record sufficient and un-foreclosing, not to adjudicate truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Answers the F-4 open question directly: the Kernel's non-negotiable job is to keep the record sufficient and un-foreclosing, not to adjudicate truth; possible-worlds semantics, the Pramana regime, statistical inference, and algorithmic knowledge are all 'regimes that read the record' rather than parts of the Kernel itself, since preservation (what must be recorded so a model can be applied later) and inference (computing what is known given a model) are different obligations with different invariants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED IN FULL — AND IT IS MY FOURTH INSTANCE OF LEVEL CONFUSION ... I-4 is NOT falsified. I misdiagnosed a LIFECYCLE gap as an ONTOLOGY falsification
a_rows_sample.statement: A prior claim that I-4 was falsified is retracted: a discharge summary is not authoritative because it was projected, but became authoritative through DERIVED -> REVIEWED -> ATTESTED -> RELEASED; governance created the authority, not the derivation. The corrected conclusion is not 'DP-2 is wrong' but 'DP-2 conflates DERIVATION with ATTESTATION'. Four prior level confusions listed: flat vs dimensional (taxonomy), artifact vs concept (existence), layer vs sibling (ontology), lifecycle vs structure (this one). A fifth was avoided by checking: the author was about to report 'there is no lifecycle', when in fact nine exist.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The precise gap — located mechanically ... THE GAP: STATUS HAS A GOVERNED STATE MACHINE. AUTHORITY DOES NOT
a_rows_sample.statement: statuses.yaml and authorities.yaml are declared orthogonal but are not equally equipped: statuses.yaml has 8 values, a progression field (order), a terminal marker (settled), a defined who-may-move role table, and lint-checkable transition guards; authorities.yaml has 5 values and none of these. Authority gates a status transition, but nothing governs how authority itself changes — no rule for who may move derived->authoritative, and no guard for it. This is exactly the I-4 problem: attestation is an authority transition (derived->authoritative); because authority transitions are ungoverned, the model cannot express 'attested', so it collapses derived into 'never authoritative'. A prior reviewer's diagnosis ('DP-2 conflates derivation and attestation') now has a mechanical cause.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 (WITHDRAWN 2026-08-02 — ILL-POSED) ... authority is TWO dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE × act-changed STANDING
a_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') is withdrawn as ill-posed: the question dissolved under discovery that authority is two dimensions in one field — immutable PROVENANCE (generated, derived) times act-changed STANDING (authoritative, provisional, historical). Provenance cannot have a state machine; standing changes by governance acts. Superseded by PM-1/PM-2, recorded in the Engineering Progression Model section 4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LG-2 | Restate DP-2 to separate DERIVATION from ATTESTATION?
a_rows_sample.statement: LG-2: should DP-2 be restated to separate DERIVATION from ATTESTATION — this is CV-1, now with a mechanical cause; routed to the ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
a_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Convergences — conclusions this track reached that the blind review reproduced (items 1-12)
a_rows_sample.statement: Twelve conclusions reproduced blind, now carrying double independent derivation: (1) KnowledgeOS is a hypothesis, gate shut, Vision unapproved; (2) 'PublicDigit is the laboratory' rejected against ADR-AIP-02, Product Primacy governs; (3) the EKP is a real governed context with named individual owner; (4) Engineering Governance is the strongest bounded context; (5) the reusable kernel list, near-identical; (6) designed-for-reuse != demonstrated-reusable (verbatim convergence); (7) individual EKP ownership is a succession risk, sharpened to 'separation of duties is real as process and unevidenced as people'; (8) three knowledge ontologies coexist unreconciled; (9) domain-free methodology sits in product paths, placement breached, plus a new instance (Platform_Capability_Pattern); (10) PMR-10's manual adoption failed, sharpened into a falsification of the Reference Architecture's protocol-suffices stance; (11) most of the 11 invariants reproduced with citations, with I-8 downgraded to invariant-in-waiting; (12) the split verdict itself (enacted internal mission vs unratified product vision).

a_rows_sample.statement: A prior 'INTENDED' evidence grade is withdrawn: intent is not evidence, and applying the repository's own rule (determine whether a proposal is a new dimension, an overloaded existing dimension, or merely another value) shows INTENDED was an overloaded existing dimension, added inside a document about evidence discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four concerns, separated as required ... A fifth concern the repository already separates ... TRUST/PROVENANCE = authorities.yaml
a_rows_sample.statement: Four concerns mapped to dimensions: EVIDENCE (D-V, new), GOVERNANCE (D-III, existing/executable via statuses.yaml), OPERATIONAL STATE (D-VI, new), INTENT (derived: f(GOVERNANCE-STATUS, OWNER), both fields already exist). A fifth concern the repository already separates, worth naming so it is not re-added later: TRUST/PROVENANCE = authorities.yaml (authoritative, derived, generated, historical, provisional), and statuses.yaml already declares status independent of authority — the repository was doing orthogonal dimensions before this commission asked for them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LG-1 was solution design, conceded ... exactly what DDD forbids. I located an asymmetry and immediately proposed its repair
a_rows_sample.statement: LG-1 ('missing transitions -> need a state machine') is conceded as solution design: an inference from a missing implementation to a model, which DDD forbids — an asymmetry was located and its repair immediately proposed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The reviewer's "that chain is QUALIFICATION, not authority" — CONFIRMED by the repository ... DERIVED → REVIEWED → ATTESTED → RELEASED describes a document becoming more trustworthy
a_rows_sample.statement: A reviewer's claim that the DERIVED->REVIEWED->ATTESTED->RELEASED chain describes qualification, not authority, is confirmed: the repository already has vocabulary for it (ES-006.1's qualification stage, ES-003 Qualification), though 'Qualification' also carries a recorded UL collision (verification activity vs promotion-ladder stage), now with a third candidate sense (the standing-assignment chain).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The progression mechanisms — inventoried as evidence (P-1..P-10)
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten progression mechanisms inventoried as observations, not assumed lifecycles: P-1 document status (8 values, order+settled+roles+guards); P-2 Authority (5 values with rank, no order/roles/guards); P-3 ES-006.1 promotion ladder; P-4 Methodology maturity; P-5 ADR-M status; P-6 Capability lifecycle; P-7 EEP (plan->...->decide); P-8 Observation Protocol (ACTIVE->CONCLUDED); P-9 Identifier lifecycles (4 series); P-10 Evidence accumulation (n=0->n=1->n>=2). A prior canonical distinction (Reference Model section 6, GEP-F1: two lifecycles never conflated, governance-artifact vs governed-work) is found before theorizing; this discovery extends that refusal rather than founding it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The flagship finding — authority is not one dimension ... authorities.yaml's own header asks TWO questions in ONE field: "how much should I trust this and where did it come from?"
a_rows_sample.statement: authorities.yaml's five values answer two different questions: 'generated' and 'derived' answer provenance (where did it come from), and can never change (origin is an immutable historical fact); 'authoritative', 'provisional', and 'historical' answer standing (how much should I trust it), and can change by a governance act. This dissolves LG-1 ('should authority have a governed state machine?') rather than answering it: half of authority cannot have a state machine (provenance never changes) and the other half changes by governance acts recorded as act-logs, not workflows. Authority = an immutable PROVENANCE fact x a mutable STANDING judgment; attestation changes standing, nothing changes provenance. This also explains why the I-4 confusion was persistent: 'derived' (provenance) was wrongly read as entailing low standing, but a signed financial statement can be derived in provenance and authoritative in standing simultaneously.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PM-1 | Should authority's two questions — provenance and standing — be separated?
a_rows_sample.statement: PM-1: should authority's two questions, provenance and standing, be separated — this supersedes LG-1, which is withdrawn as ill-posed — authority: ARB + PD-3's owner.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PM-2 | Should standing-changes (attestation, supersession) get the role/guard treatment status-changes have?
a_rows_sample.statement: PM-2: should standing-changes get the role/guard treatment status-changes have — an act-governance question, not a state-machine question — authority: ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant relationships vs implementation choices ... I-1..I-11 ... 11 invariants · 8 choices
a_rows_sample.statement: Eleven invariants traced to governed statements: I-1 Knowledge is represented by an Artifact, an Artifact is never the Knowledge; I-2 a Capability protects exactly one invariant; I-3 a Knowledge Space has a declared boundary; I-4 (underspecified, not false — holds until attestation, reclassified as a lifecycle gap not an ontology falsification, per DP-2's conflation of derivation with attestation); I-5 one authoritative artifact per topic+context (lint-enforced); I-6 the Runtime never owns Knowledge; I-7 a PKS never contains reusable Method (stated and breached); I-8 governance precedes automation; I-9 governance-status orthogonal to authority; I-10 a constitutional principle is void-overriding; I-11 (restated 2026-08-02: Knowledge does not execute, capabilities execute, knowledge constrains and informs generation — the restatement survived cross-product projection where the original would have failed). Eight implementation choices (folder mapping, markdown as representation, YAML/Mermaid, the graph's declared scope, Claude Code as the n=1 runtime adapter, frontmatter, identifier formats, Mermaid+markdown projections) may change freely without breaking the model — that distinction is what makes this a platform rather than a repository layout.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p) iff (S+(p)>0) and (S-(p)>0) within Context C ... Underdetermined: S+(p)=0 and S-(p)=0 (No evidence). a_rows_sample.statement: SPEC-CONTR-2026-v1.0 defines Contr(p) as sufficient conflicting evidence (S+(p)>tau and S-(p)>tau within a context), distinct from Underdetermined (S+=S-=0, no evidence) and Uncertain (small S+ with S-=0, low-confidence positive evidence); classifies contradictions into five structural types (Direct: p and not-p asserted in the same context; Source: two equal-authority provenance origins disagree; Rule: two derivation rules conflict; Observation: empirical observation contradicts a predicted/derived state; Interpretation: disagreement from conflicting ontology-mapping schemas), each with a formal triggering condition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Non-Explosion Postulate: for all q not in ImpactScope(p), K |-_KOS q iff (K \ {p}) |-_KOS q ... Contr_scope(p) = {p} union Dependents(p) union ConflictingSources(p) ... Query Quarantine: any query Q(q) where q in Contr_scope(p) returns state CONTRADICTION_LOCAL ... Global Immunity: any query Q(r) where r not in Contr_scope(p) executes normally, completely unaffected.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a non-explosion postulate for KnowledgeOS deduction: any query q outside a proposition p's ImpactScope must be answerable identically whether or not p is in the knowledge graph; defines the isolation boundary Contr_scope(p) as the union of p itself, its dependents, and its conflicting sources; requires queries inside the scope to return CONTRADICTION_LOCAL (with both branches' provenance) and queries outside the scope to execute completely unaffected (Global Immunity).

a_rows_sample.anchor: LifecycleState in {DETECTED, ISOLATED, TRIAGED, RESOLVED} ... Resolution Operators (delta_res): Supersede delta_super(p,P_new) Source Lineage Override ... Contextualize delta_ctx(p,C1,C2) Context Bifurcation, splits p into p(C1) and not-p(C2) ... Retract delta_retract(p,P_i) Assertion Withdrawal ... Discount delta_discount(P_i,w) Weight Discounting, applies weight penalty w in [0,1) driving support below decision threshold tau.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-state contradiction lifecycle (DETECTED -> ISOLATED -> TRIAGED -> RESOLVED) and four named resolution operators with formal signatures: Supersede (deprecates old provenance in favor of a new authoritative source, zeroing the opposing support dimension), Contextualize (bifurcates a contradictory proposition into two context-scoped, no-longer-conflicting propositions), Retract (withdraws an assertion from a specific source, zeroing its support), and Discount (applies a weight penalty driving a source's support below the decision threshold) -- with a Python ContradictionEngine reference implementation performing threshold-based detection and quarantine-scope construction.

b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.
