b_rows_sample.anchor: C* = typed inquiry + epistemic semantics ... ε_t(p)=(I_t(p),E_t(p)) where I_t(p)∈{NotAsked,Asked} and E_t(p) is defined only once inquiry has occurred. ... this candidate becomes canonical only after the minimality and empirical tests below succeed.
b_rows_sample.statement: The corrected document's working (not-yet-canonical) candidate: epsilon_t(p)=(I_t(p),E_t(p)) with I_t(p) in {NotAsked,Asked} and E_t(p) defined only once inquiry has occurred, explicitly gated on passing later minimality and empirical tests -- later found isomorphic to but less minimal than the executed Repair B (inquiry register).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The theory must prohibit an implicit transition: NotAsked → Refuted merely because p∉A. Thus: Absence cannot generate negative epistemic evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: A new transformation invariant required of the repair: absence of an assertion must never generate an implicit transition to a substantive negative epistemic value (NotAsked directly to Refuted) merely from non-membership in the assertion set -- absence cannot generate negative epistemic evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I_{K_1}(p)≠I_{K_2}(p) is sufficient to establish: K_1 ≉_O K_2, provided an O_core operation can observe that distinction. This is the exact connection between the missingness defect and the earlier equality theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: A new equality consequence: because inquiry state becomes observable under the repair, a difference in inquiry state between two knowledge states K1 and K2 is sufficient by itself to establish observational non-equivalence K1 not-approx_O K2, provided some O_core operation can observe that distinction -- connecting the missingness repair directly to the pre-existing observational-equality theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H_t=[Ask(p), NoDetermination(p)] must produce ε_t(p)=(Asked,Unknown/Absent) and not (NotAsked,∅). Therefore the repair creates a new replay invariant: Replay preserves inquiry semantics. This must be tested, not merely asserted.
b_rows_sample.statement: A new replay invariant required by the repair: replaying a history containing an Ask(p) event followed by NoDetermination(p) must reconstruct the (Asked,Unknown/Absent) state and never silently collapse back to (NotAsked,empty) -- explicitly flagged as requiring empirical testing, not mere assertion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E4-R1 — Not Asked ... E4-R2 — Asked but Absent ... E4-R3 — Asked + Unknown ... E4-R7 — Orphan ... Create an asserted document/object without semantic relationships. Expected: Orphan=True without automatically changing E(p).
b_rows_sample.statement: The corrected, executable E4 re-test protocol defines seven test records (E4-R1 through E4-R7), each specifying a setup, an expected representation and an expected semantic result, including E4-R7 (orphan) requiring that Orphan=True while the epistemic state E(p) remains unchanged -- this exact protocol is executed verbatim (7/7 PASS) in exec/test_e4_rerun.py.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F1 | Policy-free result may otherwise be interpreted as absence | F3 | Policy conflict must not collapse into unknown merely through missing policy | F5 | Missing policy must remain distinct from no inquiry | F6 | Expired policy must not be represented as nonexistent policy | F10 | Historical replay
b_rows_sample.statement: Five falsification tests (F1, F3, F5, F6, F10) are identified as affected by the missingness repair because they interact with absence, policy, or historical semantics, and must be re-run under the chosen repair -- later executed 5/5 PASS in exec/test_affected_falsification.py.

b_rows_sample.anchor: {CLOSED,PARTIAL,OPEN,BLOCKED,NORMATIVE,EMPIRICAL} ... CLOSED: Defect repaired, required test passes, evidence preserved. ... NORMATIVE: Mathematics/evidence cannot determine the answer; governance decision required. EMPIRICAL: Theory is specified but executable evidence is still required.
b_rows_sample.statement: A six-status gap classification scheme replacing the earlier vague OPEN/PARTIAL treatment: CLOSED, PARTIAL, OPEN, BLOCKED, NORMATIVE (mathematics/evidence cannot decide; governance decision required), and EMPIRICAL (theory specified but executable evidence still needed).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'M1-M7'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Status(I) in {Implemented, Partial, Specified, Missing, Unknown} ... Unknown != Missing ... Unknown != Implemented
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-value implementation-status classification for every architectural property (Implemented/Partial/Specified/Missing/Unknown), with boxed guardrails Unknown!=Missing and Unknown!=Implemented -- the distinction between Missing and Unknown is called critical.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We derive a good architectural principle and gradually begin speaking about it as though the existing system already implements it. That would be architectural hallucination ... Derived Architecture != Current Architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the risk of 'architectural hallucination' -- gradually treating a derived architectural principle as though the existing system already implements it -- and sets a strict boundary Derived Architecture != Current Architecture, requiring the current architecture to be established from evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G_i=(I_i,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a per-invariant evidence record G_i=(Invariant,Status,Owner,Mechanism,Evidence,Confidence,Gap) as the unit of the architecture audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I1 Identity ≠ State ... I15 No silent semantic strengthening ... none of these should yet be marked 'Implemented' merely because we derived them
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists a first 15-item theoretical assurance register (I1-I15: Identity!=State, historical version preservation, provenance preservation, epistemic status preservation, Unknown!=False, uncertainty preservation, model-version integrity, Inference!=Authority, Decision!=Execution, Execution!=Outcome, contradiction preservation, temporal validity, legal state transitions, pre/postconditions, no silent semantic strengthening), explicitly marked as targets not yet verified as implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_0=No evidence ... E_5=Formal verification
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-level evidence-quality hierarchy E0 (no evidence) through E5 (formal verification), via E1 claim/documentation, E2 static implementation evidence, E3 executable test evidence, E4 runtime/production evidence, worked through a provenance example progressing from documentation claim to automated evidence-chain test to production lineage recording.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I)
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates evidence strength from confidence: strong (E2) evidence from inspecting only one module may still leave confidence in system-wide enforcement low; Confidence(I) != EvidenceLevel(I).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The architecture is 82% compliant ... unless we have first defined ... population ... weighting ... independence ... evidence quality ... confidence model ... treatment of critical properties
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against stating an unsupported compliance percentage (e.g. '82% compliant') without first defining the requirement population, weighting, independence, evidence quality, confidence model and treatment of critical properties; recommends a qualitative CriticalGap measure instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G1 — Semantic gap ... G5 — Assurance gap ... These gaps can coexist
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five coexisting gap classes: G1 Semantic (software loses domain meaning), G2 Governance (authority/responsibility ambiguous), G3 Temporal (historical state not reconstructable), G4 Epistemic (evidence/uncertainty/assumptions lost), G5 Assurance (behavior may be correct but insufficiently evidenced).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation = Present but Assurance = Weak. This is not necessarily an implementation gap. It is an: Assurance Gap
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example distinguishing implementation presence from assurance: modelVersion correctly stored (Implementation=Present) but with no automated test proving it survives the workflow (Assurance=Weak) is classified specifically as an Assurance Gap, not an implementation gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ArchitectureGap != ImplementationGap != VerificationGap
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Architecture gap (design itself lacks the mechanism), Implementation gap (mechanism specified but code does not implement it correctly), and Verification gap (implementation appears correct but evidence is insufficient) as three non-identical gap types.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing ... Ownerless Invariants ... Shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a governance gap pattern where a technical mechanism (AI->Assessment->Approval) works but nobody has defined who is authorized to approve, so TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing; introduces the 'ownerless invariant' search (Owner(I)=empty set, dangerous because nobody maintains it) and its converse, the 'shared ownership' problem, where undivided shared responsibility (Owner(I)={A,B,C}) risks each team assuming another enforces the invariant -- boxed as 'shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) ... Loss(C)={p | p in CriticalProperties and p absent after transformation}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-loss function for a context-to-context contract L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C), refined to Loss(C) as the set of critical properties absent after transformation; worked example: an Assessment=(score,uncertainty,modelVersion,evidenceRef) contract sending only {score} loses uncertainty/modelVersion/evidenceRef, a Critical Semantic Gap if downstream governance requires them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ΔT=T_target △ T_actual where △ denotes symmetric difference ... Unauthorized State Transition Path
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing actual state-machine transitions T_actual from implementation and comparing to target transitions T_target via symmetric difference DeltaT = T_target triangle T_actual as a state-transition gap measure; a transition present in T_actual but absent from T_target is an Unauthorized State Transition Path warranting high priority when governance consequences exist.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t) ... Reproducibility ... Replayability ... A system may be replayable without being perfectly reproducible
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines historical replay Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t), noting exact replay (Replay(A,t)=A_t) may be impossible when external conditions change, in which case the system should preserve enough provenance to explain why; distinguishes Reproducibility (can we regenerate the same result, F(X,M)=Y again) from Replayability (can we reconstruct what happened and why), noting a system may be replayable without being reproducible (e.g. a now-defunct external service).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A new state does not necessarily know the old state ... CurrentState + HistoricalProvenance ... History must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a technically disciplined reading of an earlier 'Chapter 4' observation ('a new state does not necessarily know the old state'): rejects CurrentState=History, proposing instead CurrentState+HistoricalProvenance as sufficient for reconstructing relevant prior meaning; boxed principle: history must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Prediction -> AutomaticAuthority ... CurrentState -> AssumeCompleteHistory ... Unknown -> False ... Execution -> AssumeSuccess ... Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions
a_rows_sample.statement: States a negative-space design principle: a mature architecture must specify ForbiddenPaths as well as AllowedPaths (Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions), and lists four named forbidden implicit transitions to guard against: Prediction->AutomaticAuthority, CurrentState->AssumeCompleteHistory, Unknown->False, Execution->AssumeSuccess.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assessment -/-> Authority ... The X is important. It represents a path that the architecture must prevent
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 211 Architecture Assurance Graph with an explicit forbidden-path marker: Evidence->Assessment->Governance->Decision->Authorized Action->Execution->Outcome, with an explicit forbidden edge Assessment-/->Authority that the architecture must prevent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-01 Identity ... G-15 History ... This is the audit instrument
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 15-item provisional gap register (G-01 through G-15) as concrete audit questions (identity/state separation, historical reconstructability, provenance traceability, uncertainty preservation across boundaries, model/version provenance, inference-to-authority escalation, decision/execution separation, execution/outcome separation, illegal transition blocking, contract semantic loss, contradiction coexistence, unknown-vs-false distinguishability, automatic critical-invariant testing, single accountable ownership, prior semantic context reconstruction).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No evidence => Unknown. Not: No evidence => Missing. And certainly not: No evidence => Implemented
a_rows_sample.statement: States the methodological rule of Step 212 as most important: the gap register's rows must not be populated by imagination but from actual KnowledgeOS artifacts, with the default for absence of evidence being No evidence=>Unknown, explicitly not =>Missing and certainly not =>Implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Architectural reasoning PASS ... Gītā Chapters 1–4 COHERENT
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 verdict: architectural reasoning, DDD, mathematics, statistics, and AI dimensions each rated PASS; Gita chapters 1-4 rated COHERENT (continuing to generate architectural questions without being presented as technical proof).

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status) ... EL=∪_i EL_i
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a per-step 10-field record EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status), with the overall ledger EL as the union across all steps, turning step 213's F/D/P/U discipline into a working data structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

b_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
b_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
b_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

b_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 7 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: What was claimed? What software evidence supports it? What DDD concept does it correspond to? What mathematical object represents it? What invariant follows? What, if anything, is the Gita interpretation?
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 234 (tail) proposes the actual per-step audit framework for Steps 1-182: for each step ask what was claimed, what software evidence supports it, what DDD concept it corresponds to, what mathematical object represents it, what invariant follows, what (if any) Gita interpretation applies, and finally classify Confirmed/Partial/Intended/Contradicted/Unknown -- only after this audit should the kernel mathfrak K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) be accepted or revised.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a_i\rightarrow Evidence\rightarrow Interpretation\rightarrow Formalization, not: a_i\rightarrow DesiredTheory\rightarrow FindEvidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Central audit principle: for every architectural statement a_i from Steps 1-182, the correct direction is a_i->Evidence->Interpretation->Formalization, never a_i->DesiredTheory->FindEvidence -- this is an architecture audit, not a proof of the current theory's correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q1 -- What was actually claimed? ... Q6 -- What is the Gita relationship? The sixth field must explicitly allow: None.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six-question per-step evaluation schema: Q1 what was actually claimed, Q2 what evidence supported it, Q3 domain/DDD concept, Q4 mathematical structure, Q5 invariant, Q6 Gita relationship -- the Gita field must explicitly allow 'None', forbidding manufactured connections.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_0 -- speculation ... E_4 -- runtime/operational evidence. RuntimeEvidence > ImplementationEvidence > Documentation > Assertion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence hierarchy E0<E1<E2<E3<E4: E0 speculation (no evidence), E1 conceptual assertion, E2 documentary evidence, E3 implementation evidence, E4 runtime/operational evidence -- giving RuntimeEvidence > ImplementationEvidence > Documentation > Assertion, meaning stronger evidence for what software does, not necessarily for domain semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim_i from Implemented_i. ... If not, the result could be Intended rather than Confirmed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Claim versus implementation distinction: an architectural claim (e.g. 'KnowledgeOS guarantees provenance') must be tested by Implemented(Provenance)?, yielding Intended rather than Confirmed if unimplemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V_i\in\{C,P,I,X,U\} ... V_i=f(Claim_i,Evidence_i,Implementation_i).
a_rows_sample.statement: The five-state verdict vocabulary is retained: C Confirmed, P Partial, I Intended, X Contradicted, U Unknown, formally V_i=f(Claim_i,Evidence_i,Implementation_i).

a_rows_sample.anchor: If we do not have enough evidence: V_i=Unknown. That is a valid architectural result. Unknown>FalseConfidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Why 'Unknown' matters: the audit must resist classifying everything -- insufficient evidence should yield V_i=Unknown as a valid result, with Unknown > FalseConfidence, especially important when auditing a large AI-generated architectural history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_i=(A_i^{soft},A_i^{DDD},A_i^{math},A_i^{gov},A_i^{evidence}). ... This tells us much more than: A_i=0.9.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture alignment is explicitly multidimensional: a step can be mathematically coherent yet DDD-incoherent, software-supported yet governance-unsupported, so a single scalar score is inadequate -- instead define a vector A_i=(A_i^soft, A_i^DDD, A_i^math, A_i^gov, A_i^evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: S_i: 1 direct implementation evidence, 0.5 partial evidence, 0 no implementation evidence. But this should remain a diagnostic value -- not a universal metric.
a_rows_sample.statement: Software alignment S_i is a 3-value diagnostic (1 direct evidence, 0.5 partial, 0 none), explicitly kept as a diagnostic value, not a universal metric.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BoundedContext, Aggregate, Entity, ValueObject, DomainEvent, Policy, DomainService, ContextMapping. ... we must not force every mathematical object into an Aggregate.
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD alignment D_i inspects fit against 8 named DDD constructs (BoundedContext, Aggregate, Entity, ValueObject, DomainEvent, Policy, DomainService, ContextMapping), with an explicit warning against forcing every mathematical object into an Aggregate (a category error).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=document would have poor alignment ... K=(G,\sigma,\theta,\lambda,\pi) could have strong alignment if the software actually demonstrates these dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical alignment M_i measures how faithfully a mathematical representation captures the domain claim -- e.g. K=document has poor alignment with the current knowledge-state model, while K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) could have strong alignment only IF the software actually demonstrates these dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MaterialChange\Rightarrow GovernancePath should be tested against the actual governance mechanisms.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance alignment G_i asks whether proposed behavior is consistent with the governance architecture, e.g. testing MaterialChange=>GovernancePath against actual governance mechanisms.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_i as the interpretive relevance, not truth. ... It does not mean: The Gita proves the architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gita alignment H_i is explicitly interpretive relevance, not truth -- H_i=Strong means a meaningful interpretive parallel exists in Chapters 1-4, never that the Gita proves the architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G0 -- No meaningful connection ... G3 -- Explicit design influence. ... G3 requires evidence of actual design influence.
a_rows_sample.statement: The Gita four-layer rule (extending/refining the P1/P2/P3 vocabulary): G0 no meaningful connection, G1 analogy (conceptual resemblance), G2 interpretive principle (philosophical lens), G3 explicit design influence (architecture consciously designed using the interpretation) -- G3 explicitly requires historical evidence of actual design influence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Some engineering principles independently emerge from software architecture, mathematics, epistemology and governance; Chapters 1-4 of the Gita provide an additional interpretive lens for understanding selected principles. That is much more defensible.
a_rows_sample.statement: The G0-G3 discipline is justified as protecting the book against retroactively claiming every KnowledgeOS concept originated from the Gita, favoring the defensible framing that engineering principles independently emerge while the Gita provides an additional interpretive lens.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step | Original claim | Evidence | Software | DDD | Mathematics | Governance | Gita | Verdict. This becomes the canonical audit artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: The canonical alignment audit table for all 182 steps: columns Step, Original claim, Evidence, Software, DDD, Mathematics, Governance, Gita (G0-G3), Verdict -- designated the canonical audit artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C_{ij}=1 if Step i and Step j contain materially conflicting claims. ... {Temporal, Contextual, Terminological, Architectural, Mathematical, Implementation, Governance}.
a_rows_sample.statement: A separate contradiction register defines C_ij=1 when steps i and j materially conflict, classified into 7 contradiction types (Temporal, Contextual, Terminological, Architectural, Mathematical, Implementation, Governance) -- apparent contradiction does not necessarily mean error.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Term(t)=\{Meaning_1,\ldots,Meaning_n\}. ... Meaning(t,C_A)\stackrel{?}{=}Meaning(t,C_B). If not: ContextualPolysemy must be explicitly recorded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Terminology drift is formalized: Term(t) may map to multiple meanings across steps, tested via Meaning(t,C_A) =? Meaning(t,C_B); if unequal, ContextualPolysemy must be explicitly recorded as a direct DDD concern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K means knowledge item in one step and knowledge state in another, then K_1\neq K_2. ... a notation dictionary. K\rightarrow KnowledgeState, k\rightarrow KnowledgeItem, G\rightarrow KnowledgeGraph, ... P\rightarrow Policy.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical notation drift mirrors terminology drift (e.g. K meaning 'knowledge item' in one step vs 'knowledge state' in another gives K1!=K2); a provisional notation dictionary is proposed (K->KnowledgeState, k->KnowledgeItem, G->KnowledgeGraph, C->Context, T->Transformation, E->Evidence, A->Authority, P->Policy), pending confirmation by the Steps 1-182 audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision\leftarrow Evidence\leftarrow Observation/Requirement. ... Why do we believe our architecture? This is different from: Why does the software behave this way? Both are needed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Architecture decision provenance is a second-order provenance structure (Decision<-Evidence<-Observation/Requirement) answering 'why do we believe our architecture', explicitly distinct from and complementary to 'why does the software behave this way'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: So the reduction criterion should be: same required semantics under a well-defined mapping — not merely similar terminology.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes semantic similarity from mathematical equivalence: a legitimate reduction F:K8->K5 requires that for every required observable q, q(K8)=q_hat(F(K8)) (preservation), not merely that component names look alike (e.g. Pi~pi, or E,R->G); if such a mapping fails to preserve a required property, F is not semantics-preserving.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_8 and K_5 may describe different projections of a richer formal system ... K_8 = Ontology(U), K_5 = KnowledgeState(U), K_{230} = TransformationSystem(U). ... This is a hypothesis, not yet a theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Since both direct equivalence and both inclusion directions fail, proposes instead that K8 and K5 (and a third candidate K_230, a transformation-system kernel) may be different projections of a larger typed universe U: K8=Ontology(U), K5=KnowledgeState(U), K_230=TransformationSystem(U); explicitly labeled a hypothesis, not a theorem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Proposed three-layer architecture: Layer 1 Ontological universe O ... Layer 2 Knowledge state K ... Layer 3 Transformation/governance T ... O -> K --T--> K'.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a three-layer candidate architecture: Layer 1 Ontological universe O (Entity, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, State); Layer 2 Knowledge state K (a particular epistemic configuration over O); Layer 3 Transformation/governance T (Transformation, Policy, Authority, Validation, Evidence, Context); composing as O -> K --T--> K'. Characterized as more promising than a flat K8->K5 reduction, but still to be tested rather than declared.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The correct question is therefore not: 8->5? It is: What is the minimal typed structure capable of representing the required KnowledgeOS semantics?
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the governing research question from 'does K8 reduce to K5' to 'what is the minimal typed structure capable of representing the required KnowledgeOS semantics', with K8 and K5 becoming candidate constructions to be scored against an explicit requirement set rather than compared to each other directly.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let R = {Identity, State, Evidence, Provenance, TemporalValidity, EpistemicStatus, Relation, Transformation, Policy, Action, Uncertainty}. ... A candidate kernel K is acceptable only if there exists a representation Rep_K: R -> Structures(K) that preserves the required semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a candidate semantic requirement set R = {Identity, State, Evidence, Provenance, TemporalValidity, EpistemicStatus, Relation, Transformation, Policy, Action, Uncertainty} (explicitly not final, audit-derived) and an acceptance criterion: a candidate kernel K is acceptable only if a representation Rep_K: R -> Structures(K) exists that preserves the required semantics, enabling objective comparison of candidates.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step-243 interim verdict: Reduction NOT PROVEN; Equivalence REJECTED/UNSUPPORTED; K5⊆K8 UNPROVEN; K8⊆K5 UNPROVEN; Complementary-layer hypothesis STRONG CANDIDATE HYPOTHESIS; Final kernel NOT SELECTED.
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the step's findings into an interim verdict table: K8->K5 reduction NOT PROVEN; K8≅K5 equivalence REJECTED/UNSUPPORTED; K5⊆K8 UNPROVEN; K8⊆K5 UNPROVEN; the complementary/different-layers hypothesis rated STRONG CANDIDATE HYPOTHESIS; no final kernel selected.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet proceed to a premature Step 244. ... Construct the formal universe U and define typed categories ... Then define KnowledgeState as an actual mathematical object over that universe.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends deferring further comparison of K8/K5 until a formal universe U with typed categories (Entity, Proposition, Observation, Event, Relation, State, Evidence, Policy, Action) is constructed and KnowledgeState is defined as an actual mathematical object over U; states the overall Step-243 result as a hypothesis to carry forward and falsify, not an answer: the 8->5 reduction is not currently justified, and the evidence points toward a typed, layered architecture (ontology, knowledge state, governed transformation) as distinct but formally connected objects.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not simply write another conceptual discussion of K5 versus K8. ... Step 243 has produced a hypothesis ... That is a useful hypothesis, but it remains UNPROVEN. The next task is to try to falsify it by constructing the formal system explicitly.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids re-selecting K5 or K8, inventing a new kernel for elegance, or treating Step 243's layered-universe hypothesis as established; mandates instead that the hypothesis be tested by actually constructing the formal system (universe U, type system, K8/K5 as typed objects) rather than continuing prose discussion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Investigate whether something like this is mathematically coherent: U -> Ontology -> KnowledgeState -> Transformation -> KnowledgeState' ... Do not assume this architecture. Try to falsify it. [questions A-H]
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses eight falsification questions (A-H) against the proposed layered architecture (U -> Ontology -> KnowledgeState -> Transformation -> KnowledgeState', with auxiliary Evidence/Context/Policy/Assessment/Authority/History): can every object get exactly one type; can a KnowledgeState be constructed without already presupposing one (non-circularity); can an initial K0 exist; can a transformation operate on K0; can the resulting K1 be shown to belong to the KnowledgeState space; can validation be defined without circularity; can provenance/history be defined for the first transformation; can policy/authority remain external while still governing transformations -- any NO must record the precise obstruction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K5 may be a projection/packaging of a richer typed structure rather than a set of five primitives. That is currently the strongest mathematical hypothesis emerging from Steps 243-245. It must still be falsified.
b_rows_sample.statement: Via an independent bottom-up construction (not the top-down comparison of Step 243), reaches the same conclusion as Step 243.9-243.10: the apparent five components (G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) decompose into Content=G, Qualification=(sigma,theta,lambda), Governance=pi, so K5 may be a projection/packaging of a richer typed structure rather than five independent primitives -- named the strongest hypothesis emerging from Steps 243-245, still requiring falsification.

b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the extraction's claim 'Zero = CWA' given prior Zero experiments established Unknown != Absent, NoEvidence != EvidenceOfAbsence, Unresolved != False; instead proposes CWA as a useful comparator via the test Zero_KO =? CWA, expected to strengthen Zero by documenting why they differ. Default reasoning (CWA, circumscription, default logic, autoepistemic logic) should NOT be added as a KnowledgeOS primitive yet — there is no single universal way of reasoning from incomplete information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The fact that absence of information in an ABox only indicates lack of knowledge... is why queries are more complex than database queries. ... This is why Zero ≠ CWA. ... A concept description can also be conceived as a query ... requirements are just concept descriptions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Complete satisfaction = executable situation ... Executability means Poss(e,K) or that all actions in a history were possible. Zero is our much broader boundary/incompleteness concept. ... Zero\neq Executability ... Executable \rightarrow one possible input to a Zero analysis
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'Zero = executable situation' as 'the most important incorrect mapping in the document': executability (Poss(e,K) holding for all actions in a history) does not entail completeness of a boundary/incompleteness analysis; restates prior Zero invariants (Unknown!=Absent, NoEvidence!=EvidenceOfAbsence, Conflict!=Invalidity, UnknownDimension!=UnknownValue) and concludes Zero != Executability, with Executable at most one possible input to a Zero analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: anti-luminosity: roughly, the assumption that whenever a condition obtains, one is automatically in a position to know that it obtains. His argument uses reliability, limited discrimination and sorites-style reasoning. ... EvidenceExists(e) not=> EvaluatorCanEstablish(EvidenceExists(e)) ... Zero(K)=0 not=> Known(Zero(K)=0). This is very important for Zero.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the non-transparency principle specifically to Zero and consistency/completeness: EvidenceExists(e) not=> EvaluatorCanEstablish(EvidenceExists(e)); Consistent(K) not=> Known(Consistent(K)); Complete(K) not=> Known(Complete(K)); Zero(K)=0 not=> Known(Zero(K)=0) -- i.e. even if a knowledge base actually has zero gap, the system may be unable to know that it has zero gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge base represents what is explicitly believed; what is implicitly believed is what follows from it. ... Tell(KB,\alpha)\rightarrow KB' ... Ask(KB,\alpha)\rightarrow \{Yes,No,Unknown\} ... Only-Knowing — A formal logic for "all I know" — exactly what you need for Zero
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends Levesque & Lakemeyer's Logic of Knowledge Bases as second priority, proposing its TELL/ASK interface (with the unhedged three-valued ASK return type later replaced by Eval_c in S2520/S2521) and its 'Only-Knowing' formal logic for 'all I know' as directly relevant to the open Zero TODO and the Closed-World-Assumption question.

b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Zero invariant family with UnavailableEvidence != AbsentEvidence and NotAccessible(e) != NotExisting(e), giving a four-way split NoEvidence != EvidenceUnavailable != EvidenceForgotten != EvidenceOfAbsence, reinforcing similar findings already independently reached from Williamson and Godel in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Surprising evidence should not simply be dismissed because it conflicts with the existing knowledge structure ... Conflict \not\Rightarrow RejectNewEvidence ... Conflict\rightarrow Reassessment\rightarrow Revision rather than Conflict\rightarrow False ... contradiction is a trigger for epistemic examination, not automatically a verdict of invalidity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues against treating coherence as the sole epistemic criterion: surprising/conflicting evidence should trigger Conflict->Reassessment->Revision rather than an automatic Conflict->False verdict, directly relevant to Contr/Zero/lifecycle/revision and consistent with the project's own prior FDE research.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DO NOT PRODUCE ANOTHER ABSTRACT VERIFICATION PLAN ONLY. From this point onward, execute the verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governing transition directive: the verification programme is criticized for being increasingly precise about WHAT should be verified while still not actually verifying the complete theory end-to-end (e.g. Steps 221-222 repair SemanticIntegrity into a falsifiable form but remain NOT_EXECUTED); it is mandated to stop producing abstract plans and execute verification from this point on.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reconstruct and verify the KnowledgeOS theory from Step 1 through the latest available step ... LATER \neq AUTOMATICALLY SUPERSEDING
a_rows_sample.statement: Primary objective: reconstruct and verify the KnowledgeOS theory from Step 1 through the latest step, asking whether every claim's derivation follows, every formal object is well-defined/computable, it is empirically meaningful where claimed, and the theory remains semantically coherent under DDD/architectural interpretation -- governed by LATER != AUTOMATICALLY SUPERSEDING (a later document must explicitly resolve/replace/restrict/supersede an earlier claim before the earlier is treated as obsolete).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The approximately 200+ numbered steps are NOT independent papers. They represent an evolving research process: Question/Problem -> ... -> Later correction or generalisation.
a_rows_sample.statement: The phase_measure_theory corpus (~200+ numbered steps) is designated the primary historical source and must be read as an evolving research process (Question/Problem -> Initial hypothesis -> Mathematical/conceptual proposal -> Critique -> Refinement -> New formulation -> Further derivation -> Experiment/test -> Later correction/generalisation), not independent papers -- the task is to reconstruct the theory's genealogy and logical dependency, not merely summarize files.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Step number ... 24. Final epistemic status. Use explicit statuses such as: ESTABLISHED ... NOT_DECIDABLE_FROM_CURRENT_EVIDENCE. Do not collapse these categories.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a 24-field permanent verification record per step (step number, source, date, problem addressed, ideas/definitions/mathematical objects/assumptions/claims introduced, derivations, evidence, experiments, results, what remained open, forward resolution, current formulation, contradictions, DDD implications, mathematical/statistical/computability/architectural verdicts, final epistemic status) using an 18-value closed status vocabulary (ESTABLISHED, PROVEN, DERIVED, DEFINITIONALLY_VALID, COMPUTABLE, EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED, TESTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, PLAUSIBLE, HEURISTIC, UNVERIFIED, NOT_EXECUTED, UNDERDEFINED, ILL_TYPED, CONTRADICTED, REFUTED, NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, NOT_DECIDABLE_FROM_CURRENT_EVIDENCE) that must never be collapsed into each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. Is the definition clear? ... B. Does the derivation follow? ... C. Is the construct computable? ... D. Is it tested? Never convert a conceptual PASS into an empirical PASS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates four separately-answered questions per proposition: (A) definition clarity checklist (symbol/domain/codomain/type/scope/time/context/provenance/units all defined, no ambiguity or overloading -- mathematical elegance is not evidence of a valid definition); (B) does the derivation A|-B, B|-C actually follow, with any needed assumption exposed and never silently repaired; (C) computability, distinguishing FORMALLY_DEFINED from IMPLEMENTABLE from COMPUTATIONALLY_FEASIBLE; (D) testedness, distinguishing TESTABLE / TEST DESIGNED / TEST EXECUTED / TEST PASSED / TEST FAILED, explicitly citing the corpus's prior problem of PASS labels not backed by execution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 5.1 Type-check ... 5.2 Re-derive ... Do not accept a derivation because a source document calls it theorem/law/axiom/... 5.3 Check hidden assumptions ... 5.4 Search for counterexamples
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical verification protocol: (5.1) type-check every load-bearing statement (set membership, function domain/codomain, tuple/relation arity, operator applicability, equality/order/metric/probability/measure assumptions, algebraic structures, quantifiers) and explicitly flag ill-typed statements; (5.2) independently re-derive every claimed theorem/law/axiom/invariant/proof rather than accepting the source's label; (5.3) record every hidden assumption a derivation needs (independence, measurability, differentiability, finite variance, stationarity, determinism, closed hypothesis space, identifiability, existence of a probability distribution, completeness, consistency, non-empty state space); (5.4) actively search for counterexamples to every universal claim rather than merely describing how it could be falsified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Treat every probability/statistical statement independently. ... Especially verify whether a statistical quantity is actually defined for the kind of organizational/architectural evidence KnowledgeOS claims to process.
a_rows_sample.statement: Statistical verification protocol: check probability space, random variables, distributions, estimands/estimators, sampling/independence/dependence assumptions, likelihood, priors/posteriors, confidence/credible intervals, uncertainty propagation, missingness, identifiability, calibration, decision theory, and measurement scales; specifically verify whether a statistical quantity like P(E|H) is actually definable for organizational/architectural evidence (not imported merely because standard), marking constructions conditional/underdetermined if E, H and the likelihood-generating mechanism cannot be obtained.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Definition -> Representation -> Algorithm -> Termination -> Complexity -> Result. ... Do not accept 'computable' without identifying an actual computation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Computability verification protocol: for every major formal construct (knowledge-state construction, evidence aggregation, uncertainty representation, semantic integrity, state transitions, replay, invariant checking, conflict detection, provenance, semantic preservation, epistemic classification, decision determination, measurement functions) trace Definition->Representation->Algorithm->Termination->Complexity->Result, and where practical construct and actually test minimal executable examples/pseudocode rather than accepting an unsubstantiated 'computable' claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SI(T,K,C)=1 iff CriticalSemantics(K,C)\subseteq Recoverable(T(K)) or Loss(T,K,C) is explicitly represented. ... 1. complete preservation ... 8. non-computable recoverability ... The retention conflict MCS-2 must receive particular attention because Step 222 explicitly reports that it remains unresol
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates concrete testing of the Step 222 SemanticIntegrity repair (SI(T,K,C)=1 iff CriticalSemantics(K,C) subseteq Recoverable(T(K)) or declared Loss) against 8 named concrete scenarios (complete preservation, partial loss, declared loss, undeclared loss, empty critical-semantics set, contradictory declarations, ambiguous context, non-computable recoverability) checking well-typedness/decidability/falsifiability/usefulness/compositional stability; and mandates testing the conditional-invariant repair I_i:C_i=>R_i against the prior unconditional system per minimal-conflicting-subset (MCS) with a 5-step check (reproduce conflict, specify contexts, check mutual exclusivity, check genuine avoidance vs merely relocating the contradiction), singling out MCS-2 (retention) as explicitly still unresolved per Step 222 and requiring particular attention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Construct a KnowledgeOS Ubiquitous Language verification matrix. ... Pay special attention to the already identified: Assessment vs Assertion and Knowledge having multiple meanings.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a mandatory Ubiquitous Language / DDD verification matrix (columns: Term, Definition, Bounded Context, Type, Used consistently?, Conflicts?, Final meaning) over at least 35 named core terms (Knowledge, Information, Evidence, Observation, Assertion, Proposition, Claim, Inference, Interpretation, Truth, Belief, Confidence, Uncertainty, State, Event, Action, Transition, Decision, Determination, Authority, Policy, Context, Identity, Entity, Provenance, Lineage, Validation, Verification, Assessment, SemanticIntegrity, Conflict, Unknown, Underdetermined, Refuted, Supported, Determined), asking for each apparent synonym whether it is genuinely the same concept, flagging the already-identified Assessment-vs-Assertion collision and Knowledge's multiple meanings, and forbidding resolving terminology conflicts by simply preferring whichever term appears latest.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION vs CONTEXTUAL POLYSEMY vs VERSIONED REFINEMENT vs UNRESOLVED CONFLICT. Do not use 'different bounded context' as a universal escape mechanism.
a_rows_sample.statement: Bounded-context verification rule: every apparent mathematical contradiction must be classified as one of logical contradiction / contextual difference / lifecycle difference / abstraction-level difference / vocabulary collision / genuinely incompatible requirement, using the four-way label CONTRADICTION vs CONTEXTUAL POLYSEMY vs VERSIONED REFINEMENT vs UNRESOLVED CONFLICT; 'different bounded context' may not be used as a universal escape mechanism -- a context boundary is valid only if the differing semantics can be explicitly defined.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Original Step | Original Question | Later Step | Proposed Answer | Actually Resolves? | Evidence | Current Status ... RESOLVED ... STILL_OPEN
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates tracing every early-step question/objection/unresolved-issue/missing-definition/mathematical-difficulty/architectural-concern forward to its later proposed answer via a table (Original Step, Original Question, Later Step, Proposed Answer, Actually Resolves?, Evidence, Current Status), classified into a 10-value vocabulary (RESOLVED, PARTIALLY_RESOLVED, REFORMULATED, DEFERRED, ANSWERED_ONLY_CONCEPTUALLY, ANSWERED_BUT_NOT_DERIVED, ANSWERED_BUT_NOT_COMPUTABLE, TESTED, REFUTED, STILL_OPEN) -- rated one of the most important tasks given the theory's iterative development.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we discussed X / we proposed X / we defined X / we derived X / we proved X / we implemented X / we tested X / we observed X. These are different epistemic events.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates distinguishing theory from research process: 'discussed', 'proposed', 'defined', 'derived', 'proved', 'implemented', 'tested', and 'observed' are different epistemic events that must not be conflated -- the final theory must contain only claims whose epistemic status is correctly represented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Primitive Definitions -> Derived Definitions -> Assumptions -> Lemmas -> Propositions -> Theorems -> Algorithms -> Measurements -> Experiments -> DDD Concepts -> Architecture. ... Identify all claims that have no valid upstream foundation. These are load-bearing gaps.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates constructing a final theory dependency graph (Primitive Definitions -> Derived Definitions -> Assumptions -> Lemmas -> Propositions -> Theorems -> Algorithms -> Measurements -> Experiments -> DDD Concepts -> Architecture) with dependency/justification/assumptions/verification-status recorded on every edge; claims lacking a valid upstream foundation are to be identified as 'load-bearing gaps'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Derive the smallest set of primitives from which the surviving theory can actually be reconstructed. ... If this primitive is removed, which validated result becomes impossible to derive? If nothing depends on it, it is not part of the minimal kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Minimal-mathematical-kernel derivation rule, given known-conflicting candidate kernels: do not choose a kernel candidate by preference; instead derive the smallest primitive set by a removal test -- for each proposed primitive, ask which validated result becomes underivable if it is removed; a primitive nothing depends on is not part of the minimal kernel, and a primitive that cannot support downstream derivations is marked provisional.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not synthesize while extracting was correct for the extraction phase. ... switch deliberately into: RECONSTRUCTION + VERIFICATION.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit phase-transition ruling: Step 222's 'do not synthesize while extracting' rule was correct for the extraction phase, but having now extracted a sufficiently large amount of the corpus, the programme must deliberately switch into RECONSTRUCTION + VERIFICATION and stop indefinitely generating extraction registers.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Phase A -- Step-by-step historical verification ... Phase J -- Final reconstruction ... KNOWLEDGEOS — VERIFIED THEORY AND MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a required 10-phase execution order: A step-by-step historical verification (Steps 1->latest), B question/answer genealogy, C definition verification, D derivation verification, E computability, F statistical validity, G falsification, H Ubiquitous Language/DDD, I architecture consistency, and only then J final reconstruction of a document titled 'KNOWLEDGEOS — VERIFIED THEORY AND MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not declare the theory mathematically verified / formally proven / statistically validated / empirically validated / architecturally sound unless the corresponding evidence actually exists. ... These are successful verification outcomes.
a_rows_sample.statement: No-false-completion rule: the theory must never be declared mathematically verified, formally proven, statistically validated, empirically validated, or architecturally sound without corresponding evidence; qualified conclusions ('mathematically valid but empirically untested', 'follows conditionally on assumptions A,B,C', 'well-defined but not currently computable from available data') are explicitly named as SUCCESSFUL verification outcomes, not failures.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For each batch of approximately 5-10 steps: 1. read the source files completely; ... 10. update the Ubiquitous Language matrix where affected. ... Do not stop merely because a register has been written.
a_rows_sample.statement: Immediate-next-action mandate: process batches of ~5-10 steps at a time (read completely, create step-level verification records, trace questions forward, check definitions/derivations/computability/existing tests, identify gaps, update dependency/genealogy structures and the Ubiquitous Language matrix), then produce a concise progress checkpoint (steps/definitions/derivations verified, computations/tests actually executed, contradictions/questions resolved vs remaining, new gaps, current theory maturity) before continuing -- verification is complete only when the corpus is traced end-to-end and a final theory can be reconstructed from verified foundations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can another mathematically competent researcher take the verified definitions, follow the derivations, reproduce the computations, understand the terminology, reproduce the tests, identify the assumptions, and reach the same conclusions? If not, the theory is not yet fully verified.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governing principle / final acceptance standard for the entire verification programme: the theory counts as verified only if another mathematically competent researcher could take the verified definitions, follow the derivations, reproduce the computations, understand the terminology, reproduce the tests, identify the assumptions, and reach the same conclusions.

b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a 10-part (A-J) per-step audit record for each of Steps 221-232 read in full: (A) historical problem, (B) previous theory state, (C) new proposal, (D) derivation (with explicit NON-DERIVABLE-FROM-PREVIOUS-CORPUS labeling if it fails), (E) a 13-point definition-quality checklist, (F) computability (input/output/algorithm/termination/complexity/data/determinism/reproducibility), (G) testability, (H) a 12-value mathematical-status classification (definition/axiom/lemma/theorem/proposition/conjecture/heuristic/example/analogy/architectural rule/policy/empirical claim, with 'axiom' forbidden merely because the author calls something fundamental), (I) a 7-value evidence-class vocabulary, (J) one precise final verdict.

b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a strict 3-layer separation (Mathematical: what must be mathematically true; Domain: what the domain means; Architecture: how it could be implemented), explicitly forbidding both 'implemented therefore mathematically true' and 'mathematically elegant therefore architecturally correct' -- the relationship between layers must be evidenced bidirectionally.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Definition -> Input -> Representation -> Algorithm -> Output -> Termination -> Complexity -> Reproducibility -> Evidence. ... Where computation is impossible or undecidable, that is a valid result. Do NOT repair the theory merely to make it computable.
